issues.body:
Wiki: _Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) is an approach designed to find relationships between chemical structure (or structural-related properties) and biological activity (or target property) of studied compounds._

We need to build an interactive analysis tool to help identify point mutations that cause large change in activity. 

Input is a dataframe with the following columns: 
1. `peptide`: aligned sequences (max length N, number of unique amino acids A)
2. `activity`: measured activity

Possible outputs:

An N*A dataframe where (`n`, `a`) element contains a measure of the change of activity caused by mutating the amino acid at position `n` to `a`.

Chem: dynamic sketchers
issues.body:
Ability to integrate Datagrok with the arbitrary molecule sketcher. Such a sketcher would be implemented as part of a package, and discovered automatically at runtime. A user (or an organization) would have the ability to specify the default sketcher that should get used. The platform would use it for the following purposes automatically:
* sketching molecules in-table
* sketching molecules for similarity search
* sketching molecules for substructure search (including smarts)
* sketching molecules for any purposes (exposed to the developers via the JS API).

The base class for the sketcher is SketcherBase. Subclass it with the sketcher-specific implementation.

To use a sketcher from the JS API, use grok.chem.sketcher() method.

Here are some of the web-based sketchers that we plan to implement: 
* OpenChemLib
* Ketcher
* MarvinJS

issues.title: #175: JS API: ui.dialog's `center: true` option causes an outer dialog to close when an inner dialog is closed
issues.body:
### Description

`{center: true}` in `ui.dialog.show()` changes behaviour of the dialog with inner dialogs.

### Demo script:
```javascript
//language: javascript
//name: Template

const innerDialog = ui.dialog('Title','help url ...')
  .add(ui.p('Inner dialog content'))
  .onOK(()=>{})

ui.dialog('Title','help url ...')
  .add(ui.button("Click", () => {
  	innerDialog.show()
  }))
  .onOK(()=>{})
  .show({center: true});
```
### Steps to reproduce

1) Run the script
2) Click on the "click" button in the dialog
3) Click on the "OK" button in the _inner_ dialog

### Expected
The inner dialog closes, the outer dialog stays opened

### Actual
The inner dialog closes and the outer dialog closes too

### Additional info:
Removing `{center: true}` option returns the behaviour to nornal

issues.title: #186: JS API: ui.dialog's `center: true` option causes an outer dialog to stay blocked when the inner dialog closes
issues.body:
### Description

`{center: true}` in `ui.dialog.show()` for the inner dialog blocks its appearance for the second time

### Demo script:
```javascript
//language: javascript
//name: Template

const innerDialog = ui.dialog('Title','help url ...')
  .add(ui.p('Inner dialog content'))
  .onOK(()=>{})

ui.dialog('Title','help url ...')
  .add(ui.button("Click", () => {
  	innerDialog.show({center: true})
  }))
  .onOK(()=>{})
  .show({center: true});
```
### Steps to reproduce

1) Run the script
2) Click on the "Click" button in the dialog
3) Click on the "OK" button in the _inner_ dialog
4) Click on "Click" button in the _outer_ dialog

### Expected
The inner dialog shows again

### Actual
The inner dialog is not shown

### Additional info:
Removing `{center: true}` option returns the behaviour to nornal

#204: JS API: add the feature to control the limits on plots' axes
issues.body:
### Context

We use the different kinds of plots everywhere on the platform. Most of them have axes with visual ticks on them. However, the limits (the minimum and maximum values on the axes) are computed automatically based on the input data.

### Problem

Sometimes it is important to control the limits manually. For example:
1) The values more than particular value are not in the focus of interest. Here it is useful to set the maximum value of the axis.
2) The values have a traditional minimum value (0 for absolute temperature).  Here it is useful to set the minimum value of the axis.

### Proposal 

Add the API to control the initial axes' limits. Only initial limits should be affected since a user can zoom in and out freely.

issues.title: Chem: Mini research about similarity metrics
issues.body:
Here are what I found during my research about similarity metrics.

Dice - used in statistics to gauge similarity of two samples doi: 10.1016/S1076-6332(03)00671-8
Cosine - finds cosine angle between two vectors, which is very popular
Kulczynski similarity index - the proposed method support comparison with multiple ground truth segmentations and   takes into account the irregularity of meshes
Asymmetric - asymmetric similarity (aka The Tversky index) measure on sets that compares a variant to a prototype.  The Tversky index can be seen as a generalization of the Dice coefficient and the Tanimoto coefficient (aka Jaccard index).
 
SIde note, RDKIT can calculate the following similarity models: Tanimoto, Dice, Cosine, Sokal, Russel, Kulczynski, McConnaughey, and Tversky. 

In the paper "A comparison of 71 binary similarity coefficients: The effect of base rates" by Brusco. M. et all, the authors clustered binary similarity metrics by how they are affected by the base rates (percentage of ones). 
![journal pone 0247751 t003](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26120466/151978782-7b805175-1eb7-4704-8c3c-6eb541a1eaac.PNG)
Source - https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0247751

In the paper "A generalizable definition of chemical similarity for read-across" by Floris. M. et all, the authors report comparison of multiple combinations of binary fingerprints and similarity metrics for computing the chemical similarity in the context of two different applications of the read-across technique. They came up with the top 10 results for fingerprints/similarity metrics combinations.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26120466/151980423-bdd982a2-2a3c-4c72-8a98-acf95f09ec4d.png)
"The best coefficients found in combination with the fingerprints are 37 (Maxwell-Pilliner), 34 (Cohen), 18 (Rogot-Goldberg), 42 (CT4), 13 (Sokal-Sneath), 1 (simple matching)"
Source - doi:10.1186/s13321-014-0039-1

issues.body:
Issue is reproduced on https://dev.datagrok.ai/

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open any table (e.g. from file)
2. Open filters panel
3. Apply some filtering (e.g. select some items/change range for the 1st of the default filters)
4. Close filters >> *filtering is un-applied*
5. Open filters again >> *filtering is applied again*
6. Reset filters >> *filtering is un-applied in current view*
7. Clone the current view

**Expected results:** no filters applied in the cloned view. Behaviour on closing filters should be the same as before: filters are un-applied when filters panel is closed.
**Actual results:** filters are applied in the cloned view. Behaviour on closing filters has changed for both views: filtering is not un-applied when filters panel is closed.

issues.title: #452: JS API: DataFrame data full replace method is required
issues.body:
### Context

We have multiple viewers that are connected to the dataframes. When we create a new DF and connect it to the existing viewer, we lose the subscription we had on the old DF. 

Manual values setting using `addRow`/`addColumn` or `set` methods are very inconvenient - they require to row/column count to be identical. 

### Problem

```
let t = grok.data.testData('demog', 10);
let v = grok.shell.addTableView(t);

t.onCurrentCellChanged.subscribe((_) => grok.shell.info(`Cell: ${t.currentCell.rowIndex}, ${t.currentCell.column.name}`));

let t2 = grok.data.testData('geo', 20)
v.dataFrame = t2
```
In the script above, we lose the `onCurrentCellChanged` subscription. It would be great not lose it, meaning that there is need to replace all the data in `t` with any data we want.

### Proposal 

Add the API to completely replace the data in DF without changing its subscriptions. Proposed method should fire `onValuesChanged` and `onDataChanged` events.

issues.title: Compute: "Load file" button
issues.body:
External input data often comes in an Excel file with several sheets.

Currently, loading a file from disk or from a separate file storage in Datagrok is only possible with drag-and-drop of the file into the platform, and then matching multiple dataframes extracted from the Excel in input dataframes' dropdowns inside the model's input interface.

There are several drawbacks to this:

1. Requires several actions from the user instead of one focused action, and requires the user to be educated on doing it

2. May introduce an inconsistent state in some of the UIs, where the dataframe selection dropdown is empty, and increases the number of UI states in general

3. Complicates matters when the user works with several input files at once. For example, when consecutively editing the template file on his/her computer and then loading it into the model again and again. In this scenario, several dataframes of identical names, corresponding to sheet names, will appear, even if the entire input file was named distinctively. This makes it hard to orient within these many dataframes

There is a consistent request from the users and stakeholders to cover this scenario via a single button.

We need to come up with an agreed design for such button.

DataFrame: strongly-typed columns
issues.body:
Let's make our columns strongly-typed, just like in the core.

```
let col = dataFrame.columns.addNewString('foo');
let x = col.get(0);  // inferred type: string (but really it could be null; check it by calling col.isNone(i) first)
col.set(0, null);  // accepts null
```

Important implementation detail: `get` returns `T`, but `set` accepts `T | null`. This is done to make the client code look cleaner and get rid of null checks, since in most cases the application programmer knows in advance that the column does not contain empty values (and if it does, a separate check col.isNone is typically performed). Keep in mind that get(i) will still return null if there is no value.

issues.title: Structure queries
issues.body:
Out-of-the-box, you can paste SMILES, MOLBLOCK, and InChi keys into the input field, and the sketcher
automatically translates it to a structure. In addition to that, you can make sketcher understand
other structure notations (such as from your company's internal database of structures) by registering
a function annotated in a special way. The following example provides support for Chembl. The important
tags are:
* `--meta.role: converter`: indicates that such a function serves as a value converter
* `--meta.inputRegexp: (CHEMBL[0-9]+)`: RegExp that is evaluated to check if this function
  is applicable to the user input. The captured group (in this case the whole input) is then
  passed to this function as a parameter. 
* `--output: string smiles { semType: Molecule }`: should return string with the semType `Molecule`

```
--name: chemblIdToSmiles
--meta.role: converter
--meta.inputRegexp: (CHEMBL[0-9]+)
--connection: Chembl
--input: string id = CHEMBL1185
--output: string smiles { semType: Molecule }
select canonical_smiles from compound_structures s
join molecule_dictionary d on s.molregno = d.molregno
where d.chembl_id = @id
```

issues.title: Controlling sizes/colors of the scatter plot points
issues.body:
### Background:

There is a feature of configuring scatter plot's points size according to the `float`/`int` columns. 
There is need to configure scatter plot's points size and colors depending on categorical columns. For example, based on boolean/string values. This feature will add a lot of customization possibilities.

Example of possible customization - different size for special point on the plot: 
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5558521/172642455-4ab6299c-8c41-4e19-a0b2-8f4cd53884cb.png)

### Proposed solution

We have similar feature for assigning particular point markers according to the categorical values. I propose add similar functionality for marker's size and color.
It works this way:
```
myColumn.meta.markers.assign('synthetic', DG.MARKER_TYPE.STAR);
```

New API could work this way:

```
myColumn.meta.colors.assign('synthetic', '#FFFFFF');
myColumn.meta.colors.assign('natural', '#000000');

myColumn.meta.sizes.assign('synthetic', 20);
myColumn.meta.sizes.assign('natural', 5);
```

issues.title: File entity introduction
issues.body:
### Background 

A lot of users used to store all the data in files, e.g. several DFs in single Excel file. Right now platform forces them to use these files as arrays of distinct DFs. This breaks their usual behaviour and messes in the user's workspace if file with 5+ DFs is uploaded.

### Proposed solution

Add new entity called "File" or smth similar with new input field. This field should allow to upload files (Excel or CSV) without adding them into workspace and properly parsing them into array of DFs.

Proposed API is similar to API of `ui.tableInput` but returns array of DFs:
```
ui.fileInput("Upload existing files", null, null, (dfs: DG.Dataframe[]) => { console.log(dfs.length, ' DFs are uploaded') })
```

### Details after sprint planning
1) JS API for file handlers
2) InputBase for binary with name
3) Handling DFs with no addition to workspace

issues.title: #720: Browse: Add 'open on double click' feature to open files displayed in the search results panel
issues.body:
RE: Opening files in **Files** 

To open a file, users navigate the files tree, locate the file they want to open, then double-click to open (a single click brings up a file preview in the preview pane).  

Instead of navigating the file tree, users can search files available to them by typing a file's name in the search box; the matching files are displayed in the search panel. However,  users can't open files displayed in the search panel. The only action available to users from the search panel is to preview a file's content (upon single click).

issues.title: #721: Layout: Before applying a Layout, allow users to preview the result first, and then decide if they want to proceed (or provide an option to revert changes)
issues.body:
RE: Applying **Layouts**

Users can see a list of **Layouts** that apply to their data sets by expanding the **Layouts** menu on the **Toolbox**. When users click on one of the suggested **Layouts** on the **Toolbox**, that **Layout** is immediately applied to their data set. Users have no way of knowing this is coming, nor that they won't be able to revert the change. 

It would be useful to users to be able to preview the result first, and then decide whether they want to apply the **Layout** or keep the current **View**. Alternatively, provide an option to revert changes and go back to the original **View** after the **Layout** has been applied.

issues.title: bio: WebLogo: Fix for window.devicePixelRation not equal 1
issues.body:
If window.devicePixelRatio > 1, then the canvas layout is calculated like with fitArea=true or fitArea=false randomly, so the Logo picture jumps in height, possibly because of the dependence of the previous state.
![Image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3798326/193285698-19d9d642-ffaf-408f-b23e-ebce4a9f8089.gif)

If window.devicePixelRatio < 1, then canvas layout calculation depends on the previous viewer state, and repeatedly changing control width leads to a continuous increase of visible position width.
![Image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3798326/193285731-b4f17de9-b027-4e30-b53b-7a99bd84f02f.gif)

window.devicePixelRation can be changed by page zoom in browser, and checked in console

issues.title: Extended color picker (hex/RGB codes, common/corporative/recent colors)
issues.body:
**Color Picker**

Color Picker box appears in a new dialog (this behavior should be consistent for all data types - numeric, string, etc.).

Users can choose from six different color sources:

_**Standard colors: (must)**_
- Blue #73AFF5
- Yellow #FFDF5B
- Red #FF5140
- Green #50AF28
- Gray #D9D9D9

**_Corporate colors: (optional)_**
- See screenshot attached to the ticket

_**Color box (must)**_

_**Eyedropper tool (optional)**_

_**Hex-code entry (must) and RGB entry (optional):**_ 
- Hex code is default. Users can switch to RGB.

_**Recent colors: (must)**_
- Colors selected from either the color box, eyedropper or by hex-code/RGB entry are displayed in a "Recent" section
- Max 6 recent colors (could also be 5 if we go with Standard colors only) can be displayed until they will get overwritten again
- Recent colors should be available on application level
- For all color sources, the color hex-code of the selected color is displayed.

**Pick Up/Apply Coloring**

Add ability to copy existing colour-coding (conditional and catagorical) from one column to another or to more than one.

Our proposal: Pick Up/Apply allows users to pick up the whole configuration (colors and formatting) of one column and apply it again to one or multi-selected columns.

3. Configure viewer so that showing legend is applicable (e.g. color by column for scatter plot, or split by column for line chart)
4. Set-up in-viewer filter so that there are no data shown in viewer
5. Change in-viewer filter so that there is some data shown in viewer
**Expected results:** Legend should be shown.
**Actual results:** Legend is still hidden.
6. Save layout
7. Close and open the same table and re-apply layout
**Expected results:** Legend is shown, legend is synchronised with in-viewer filter and is not showing categories that are hidden on the plot.
**Actual results:** Legend is shown, but it is not synchronised with in-viewer filter. All existing categories are shown instead.

issues.title: #1362: #1362: Chem: RDKit minimal lib - R-groups
issues.body:
Datagrok uses [RDKit minimal lib](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/tree/master/Code/MinimalLib) for cheminformatics related calculations. Minimal lib is limited to a subset of features presented in [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org/) which is usually wrapped and used in Python. Some more features will be useful in the minimal lib. One of them are features essential for R-groups analysis. In Python RDKit they are used as:
[Chem.ReplaceCore](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.html#rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.ReplaceCore)
[Chem.GetMolFrags](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.html#rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags)

Implement these both functions RDKit minimal lib using c++

Add this functionality to [JS wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/master/Code/MinimalLib/jswrapper.cpp) and to [CFFI wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/5d0be00f8dee7d2098944b83c3bb08adb01504ec/Code/MinimalLib/cffiwrapper.cpp)

issues.title: #1400: Chem: RDKit minimal lib - reactions
#1401: Chem: RDKit minimal lib - Murcko Scaffolds and FromInchi
issues.body:
Datagrok uses [RDKit minimal lib](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/tree/master/Code/MinimalLib) for cheminformatics related calculations. Minimal lib is limited to a subset of features presented in [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org/) which is usually wrapped and used in Python. Some more features will be useful in the minimal lib. Basic features to support cheminformatics are among them. In Python RDKit they are used as:
[MolFromInchi](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.inchi.html)
[MurckoScaffoldSmiles](https://rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.html)

Implement these both functions RDKit minimal lib using c++

Add this functionality to [JS wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/master/Code/MinimalLib/jswrapper.cpp) and to [CFFI wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/5d0be00f8dee7d2098944b83c3bb08adb01504ec/Code/MinimalLib/cffiwrapper.cpp)

issues.title: #1414: Usage Analysis
issues.body:
Usage Analysis (UA) app provides convenient UI for analyzing platform usage, including sessions, events, packages, errors, and more. 

Here are some of the typical questions that the application answers:
* Usage summary (#unique users, new users, etc)
* Who is using a particular package?
* What does a particular user/group use?
* Which errors were reported recently? Are they known or new errors? Is there a pattern to a specific error? Can I see complete session log?
* Can I see a complete log for any session?
* What are the parameters of the particular event?
* What are the most popular actions for the package of interest?

Important features
* User-friendly, intuitive UI
* Global filter on group, date range, and package
* Routing
* Ability to report an error to a tracker (github?)

Performance considerations
* The UA widget should load really fast; likely, both server- and client- side caching would be needed
* We might need to speed up the database by adding indexes, if necessary

issues.title: Turning off filters does not disable filtering if another view contains same column in filters panel
issues.body:
v.1.9.2, 1.11.3

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open a table
2. Open filters
3. Make sure there are some columns added to filters
4. Clone current view
5. Set up filtering so that some rows are filtered out
6. Turn off all filters
**Expected results:** all filtering is turned off, all rows are displayed.
**Actual results:** turning off filters has no effect on rows displayed.
7. Turn on filters again
8. Turn off some individual filter
**Expected results:** rows filtered out by this individual filter should be shown again.
**Actual results:** turning off individual filter has no effect on rows displayed.

Issue happens only for columns present in both views.


This issue looks like a synchronisation bug. Syncing state of on/off checkboxes for all filters and for individual filters across views should probably solve it.

issues.title: Peptides: cluster deletion bug
issues.body:
Platform version: 1.12.0
Package version: 1.6.1
Steps to reproduce: select a custom cluster for deletion and click delete button
Expected behavior: cluster is deleted and removed from Logo Summary Table. The Distribution widget is updated.
Actual behavior: cluster is deleted, however it is remaining in the Logo Summary Table. The Distribution widget is not updated.

issues.title: Trellis plot with bar charts: not all data is shown until bar chart is clicked
issues.body:
**Steps to reproduce:** 
1. Open SPGI
2. Add Trellis plot
3. Main configuration X: Scaffold names, Y: Series (default one)
4. Switch to bar charts
5. Inner viewer configuration Value: CAST Idea ID, Split: Stereo Category (default)

**Expected results:** Complete data on bar charts should be shown at once.

issues.title: #1562: Chem: R-groups (c++ to JS)
issues.body:
Datagrok uses [RDKit minimal lib](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/tree/master/Code/MinimalLib) for cheminformatics related calculations. Minimal lib is limited to a subset of features presented in [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org/) which is usually wrapped and used in Python. Some more features will be useful in the minimal lib. 
Implement R-groups analysis in RDKit minimal lib using c++. 
In Python RDKit we implemented it as:
[find R-group](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/blob/master/packages/Chem/scripts/find_rgroups.py)

Expected JS signature is:
find_rgroups(molecules: string[], core: string): { [fragment: string] : string[]; }(see line 73 in Python script)

Add this functionality to [JS wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/master/Code/MinimalLib/jswrapper.cpp) and to [CFFI wrapper](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/5d0be00f8dee7d2098944b83c3bb08adb01504ec/Code/MinimalLib/cffiwrapper.cpp)

Example of usage:
![Image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57249456/216430708-d0a5c68a-b5f3-4eee-8a48-22ecdd1b8818.gif)

issues.title: Chem - Descriptors fail on sparse dataset
issues.body:
Most Chem augmentation functions (Chem | Descriptors and Chem | Map Identifiers) fail when a record lacks a Structure or potentially if the function returns nothing.

This is reproducible by loading the ‘sar-small.csv’ sample file and then by adding an empty row. Use the plus symbol at the bottom of the table. Then run any of the Descriptor functions or Map Identifiers functions. You will receive an error similar to “Row counts don’t match (data frame: 201, column: 150)”

I don’t believe this is expected behavior. If a row lacks a structure (or is invalid) then that row should be skipped and the entire operation should succeed. This will allow users to have sparsely populated compound datasets.

Similar to this issue is the generation of 'Chem | Fingerprints". The empty row should not produce a fingerprint but seems to with a value of “2048 bits, 0 set”.

issues.title: DG 1.13.13: a height of 0 is being passed to OffscreenCanvas
issues.body:
@StLeonidas @MariaDolotova While testing DG 1.13.13 with `Chem. 1.5.28` we have run into this error:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5244385/233440968-82701cc3-8286-4a86-8c35-3f1a1b01a391.png)
What I believe happens is that `drawMoleculeToCanvas()` is passed a `0` height parameter.
In fact, first an exception is thrown here:
https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/blob/638da4c874add9f4cbd5fde601c692f8b8ec52b0/packages/Chem/src/utils/chem-common-rdkit.ts#L132
which I can easily reproduce as follows in the console:
```
let width = 300;
let height = 0;
offscreenCanvas = new OffscreenCanvas(width, height);
mol = chem.getRdKitModule().get_mol('C');
mol.draw_to_canvas_with_highlights(offscreenCanvas, JSON.stringify({width, height}))
Uncaught 1607600
```
Then, since the molecule has failed to render, the `Chem` calls `drawErrorCross` and draws a cross on the `OffscreenCanvas` with `0` height, however, then `getImageData` fails:
https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/blob/638da4c874add9f4cbd5fde601c692f8b8ec52b0/packages/Chem/src/utils/chem-common-rdkit.ts#L196
```
IndexSizeError: Failed to execute 'getImageData' on 'OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D': The source height is 0.
```
This can be easily reproduced in the console with the following command:
```
offscreenCanvas.getContext('2d').getImageData(0, 0, width, height);
```
So I believe you need to investigate why `drawMoleculeToCanvas()` is passed a `0` height, and possibly clip the minimum width and height to 1 as a failsafe mechanism in case something goes wrong upstream and `0` width or height are passed.

issues.title: Filter's missing values settings are not properly synced between different tabs/views
issues.body:
**Case 1:** 
1. Open a table, e.g. SPGI
2. Add another view in the same table
3. Open filters in both views
4. View 1: add numerical column, and set one of the following options:
'filter out missing values'
'show only missing values'
5. View 2: add the same numerical column to filters
**Expected results:** Adding the same column to filters in another view should not change filters state.
**Actual results:** missing values settings are reset:
If 'show only missing values' was selected > filter is reset completely.
If 'filter out missing values' was selected > only range set is kept, missing values are not filtered out anymore.

**Case 2:**
1. Two views are opened
2. Same numerical filter is present in both views
3. Filter is switched from 'show only missing values' to 'Keep missing values' on one of the views
**Expected results:** filter is updated in the 2nd view too.
**Actual results:** in some cases, the range filter is not updated in another view if the setting was changed from 'show only missing values' to 'Keep missing values' on one of the views

issues.title: Viewer docked at the left or at the top is sometimes unexpectedly hidden
issues.body:
**Preconditions:**
Open SPGI table.

**Case 1: docking viewer**
1. Add a viewer
2. Dock it to the left or to the top
**Expected results:** viewer is still visible after docking.
**Actual results:** viewer is hidden.
![2023-09-04_13-10-16 (1)](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/assets/15780643/952807f7-bd4d-435e-958e-95b29373b143)
Issue happens more often for docking to the left, but sometimes can be also reproduced for docking to the top of the page.

**Case 2: applying saved layout**
1. Add a viewer to the left side of screen or open filters
2. Save layout
3. Decrease window width in any way (resize browser window, change screen resolution or open browser console at the right)
4. Re-apply saved layout
**Expected results:** All viewers and filters should be visible when layout is re-applied.
**Actual results:** viewer or filters docked to the left are hidden:
![2023-09-04_13-26-14 (1)](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/assets/15780643/1de2ac78-25d7-4c1c-940e-164087b61818)
This case is the most likely to happen for filters, because their default position is on the left.

issues.title: #2491: Docking: Docker container for Autodock
issues.body:
# Background
This ticket covers the development of the Docker container for the Autodock plugin. See the full description in the parent ticket.

# Scope of work
The Docker container should contain the autogrid4 and Autodock-GPU utilities and all required scripts. Container functions:

## Run grid calculations for macromolecule. 
* Input:
    * Macromolecule pdb/pdbqt file
    * Grid parameters file
* Output: 
    * Calculation log
    * Grid files are stored in the docker container/volume. There is no need to return it to the client
* Cache calculated grids (using Docker volumes or similar):
    * On the first run, save grid files to local storage (suggest Docker volumes)
    * Bypass calculations for the macromolecules that already have the grids.
    * Accept a flag to force grid re-calculation.

## Run the docking calculation for the small molecule and the macromolecule. 
If the macromolecule grids are not available, run grid calculation first. The docking calculations should use the GPU version of Autodock.
* Input
    * small molecule pdb/mol2 file
    * macromolecule file name
* Output
     * Full docking log file
     * molecule conformation in the pdbqt file (extracted from the docker logs)

issues.title: #2492: Autodock plugin
issues.body:
# Background
The epic covers the development of the docking plugin for Datagrok using the Autodock4 engine.
The discussion thread: https://datagrok.slack.com/archives/G01BZ4Y776E/p1698873693338189 

# Use cases
* You have the macromolecule (receptor) PDB file and a dataframe with small molecules.
* You run docking of the molecule set to the macromolecule.
* Autodock returns a set of possible 3D conformations for each small molecule. 
* Datagrok joins all docked conformations in the single dataframe and displays it
* You can explore the docking results using the existing Datagrok docking results viewer.


# Technical realization
We use for the docking the combination of the original Autodock tool (https://autodock.scripps.edu/download-autodock4/) and the GPU-optimized version of Autodock: https://github.com/ccsb-scripps/AutoDock-GPU 

To perform the docking, we need to do the following:
* Specify the dataframe column containing small molecules and choose the pre-configured macromolecule via input UI: https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2568
* Perform the docking https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2491
    * Calculate atomic grids using the autogrid4 utility. This is a time-consuming step running on a single CPU. We cache the grids in the contained, so subsequent runs with the same macromolecule don't require grids calculation.
    * Convert small molecule to pdbqt format
    * Perform docking using the Autodock-GPU utility
* Visualize results
    * Open the macromolecule on the 3D viewer
    * Parse the Autodock log and extract the pdbqt records for the small molecule (simple shell script implemented): https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2481
    * Show the molecule conformation on the 3D viewer. TODO: discuss the way to switch conformations.

# Improvements
* Handle the failures in the docking calculations: https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2732
* File preview handler for autogrid configuration files: https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2740
* Notification in the "poses" column for the failed run: https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/issues/2741

issues.body:
1.17.3, 1.16.3, powergrid 1.2.1, 1.1.33

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open a table

3. Save layout
4. Reapply saved layout
5. Unpin all columns
6. Save layout again
7. Re-apply layout saved on previous step

**Expected results:** Pinning and un-pinning columns should not unexpectedly hide row headers.
**Actual results:** Row header disappears. Column properties still have 'Show row header' checked.

issues.title: RdKitService stays unresponsive as terminateFlag is not reset after substructure search has completed
issues.body:
We have noticed that under certain circumstances similarity search would not work straight after loading an analysis.
This can be consistently reproduced on an analysis containing ~1300 molecules with the following workflow.
Commands below need to be typed in the Edge developer console.

1. Load the analysis -> Load with cached data (makes no difference for the bug, but it is faster)
2. Delete any cached columns if present:
```
tildeCols = Array.from(grok.shell.tables[0].columns).filter(c => c.name.startsWith('~'))
tildeCols.map((c) => c.name)
(2) ['~Structure.Pattern', '~Structure.canonicalSmiles']

tildeCols.map((c) => grok.shell.tables[0].columns.remove(c.name))
(2) [ColumnList, ColumnList]

tildeCols = Array.from(grok.shell.tables[0].columns).filter(c => c.name.startsWith('~'))
tildeCols.map((c) => c.name)
[]
```
3. Open Structure search, choose similarity search, draw something, then Exit->Discard. This will create a `~Structure.Morgan` cache column:
```
tildeCols = Array.from(grok.shell.tables[0].columns).filter(c => c.name.startsWith('~'))
tildeCols.map((c) => c.name)
['~Structure.Morgan']
```
4. Now open Structure filter, sketch something, then cancel. This will create `~Structure.Pattern` and `~Structure.canonicalSmiles` cache columns:
```
tildeCols = Array.from(grok.shell.tables[0].columns).filter(c => c.name.startsWith('~'))
tildeCols.map((c) => c.name)
(3) ['~Structure.Morgan', '~Structure.Pattern', '~Structure.canonicalSmiles']
```
5. Now, Save the analysis.
6. Do a hard refresh of the browser (Empty cache and hard refresh).
This time, you need to Load with Fresh Data.

issues.title: #2573: RFC: Universal way of performing dimensionality reduction on multiple columns
issues.body:
Purpose:

* To have a unified method for dimensionality reduction that will support multiple columns and would be easily extended with supported column types from different packages.

Problem:

* Datagrok currently can perform dimensionality reduction on biological sequences, molecules or numbers separately. Each of these methods are separately placed in corresponding packages, and there is a lot of code duplication. 
* There is an increased interest in being able to process different columns and produce their embeddings in 2d space. In current realization of code, one would need to duplicate similar code sequence/chem space in order to add support for particular column. 
* We cannot currently do dimensionality reduction for an arbitrary set of columns, including string types (for instance AGE / HEIGHT / SEX)
* We don't have "find similar" functionality based on the arbitrary set of columns. This might be useful as a context panel.

Proposed Solution:

* Create a unified function for performing dimensionality reduction, that would dynamically know which columns are supported and what preprocessing/distance functions they support. these preprocessing functions would be picked up from any installed package, and then called on column before calculating embeddings. For example, when performing sequence space, first step is encoding of sequences and constructing monomer substitution matrix. In proposed solution, in order to add support for macromolecule columns, only thing needed is to expose a preprocessing function in bio that encodes sequences. For aggregating different columns, ui will include items grid editor which will allow to add multiple columns, including its preprocessing function, distance function and weight used for distance aggregation. 

Benefits:

* Much less code, less needed to test and maintain. 
* Easier way of adding new supported function, easier way of extending.
* Support for multiple columns together

![image](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/assets/943403/6d9ee9c6-5f06-4e21-8522-b37b32c07f27)

issues.title: #2627: RFC: Sticky Meta
issues.body:
This document outlines the rationale, requirements, and proposed technical implementation of the “DB Properties” feature.

# Context and Goals
Datagrok has a concept of entities. Among other features, it enables each internal object (dataset, connection, query, function, user, group, etc) to be associated with the arbitrary metadata (at this moment the UI only supports strings). The goal of this initiative is to improve the existing functionality (more types, better UI, powerful search) and extend this functionality to objects that are stored externally. This would enable end users to quickly build lightweight solutions (with no coding required) to a certain kind of problems that are traditionally solved by the IT in a resource-intensive way (extending existing databases, providing the APIs, building the apps for the end users, maintaining it, etc).

**Use case 1:** Peter, the head of cheminformatics at BostonMol, wants to run a hit triage campaign. He wants BostonMol’s chemists to be able to provide “good/neutral/bad” ratings to any of the molecules in the proprietary database. Also, no matter where the dataset came from (db / file / web service), we want to be able to see a molecule's rating in the context panel, and retrieve the corresponding ratings for all molecules in the dataset. To do that, Peter, through the UI, creates a schema {name: “Hit Triage”, appliesTo: {semType: “BMol”}} with the following property: { name: “Rating”, choices: [“good”, “neutral”, “bad”] }. Since molecule ids are detected as the “BMol” semtype, this is enough for Datagrok to put everything together.

**Use case 2:** Peter runs a database query and wants to annotate rows in such a way that these annotations would be visible next time he or anyone else runs this query, or opens a dataset with the similar structure. From the results view, he clicks Data | Annotate…, and either selects an already existing schema, or creates a new one, creating the desired properties as well. Then, he chooses key columns along with the way they should be matched (multiple checkboxes: by name, by tag values). Once he clicks OK, corresponding columns are created, and the values are editable in the grid.

# Implementation

## Database representation

We would reuse and extend existing powerful implementations of entities, properties, dynamic inputs, and semantic types.

Property table defines metadata (not value!) associated with a property. It would be mapped to the existing class Property. Here are some of the fields:

**properties table**
```
id: uid
schema_id: uid
name: string
caption: string  // name to show in the UI
category: string  // for automatically generated UI
description: string  // shown in the tooltip, etc   
propertyType: string  // int, float, bool, string, datetime, list
semType: string
choices: list<string> // controlled dictionary of allowed values
format: string
min: float
max: float
validators: list<string>  // GrokScript expressions
```

The actual values would reside in the property_values table (plus a record in the entities table):

**property_values** tables
```
entity_id: uid
property_id: uid
value: dynamic
```

Often, more than one field is required. To address that, each property is associated with the schema (for developers, think of schemas as classes, and properties as fields). Schemas support inheritance that allows us to reuse common properties:

**schemas** table
```
id: uid
parent_schema_id: uid
name: string
appliesTo: json  // a set of column tags. Evaluated with the AND operator. 
                          // Example: { semType: “BMol”, campaign: “Hit Triage”}
entity_types table
id: string
name: string
description: string
```

**entity_types_schemas** table
```
entity_type_id: uid
schema_id: uid
```

Schema itself is an entity. The privileges (View / Edit) associated with it define whether the user can view the properties, or edit them. 

Example: Mary is giving the “good” ratting for the “ccc” BMol molecule and “bad” rating for the “c” molecule. It would go to the following tables:


**entity_types**
```
Id: 0, name: “semType=BMol”
schemas
id: 1, name: “Mol Rating”
entity_types_schemas
entity_type_id: 0, schema_id: 1
properties
id: 2, schema_id:1, property_type: “string”, semType: “rating”, name: “rating”, choices: [“good”, “neutral”, “bad”]
id: 20, schema_id:1, name: “chemist”, propertyType: “string”
entities
id: 3, entity_type_id: 0, key: “ccc”
entities
id: 31, entity_type_id: 0, key: “c”
property_values
id: 40, entity_id: 3, property_id: 2, value: “good”
property_values
id: 41, entity_id: 3, property_id: 20, value: “Mary”
property_values
id: 42, entity_id: 31, property_id: 2, value: “bad”
property_values
id: 43, entity_id: 31, property_id: 20, value: “Mary”
```


## JS API

In addition to self-managing, we need the ability to programmatically create, edit, delete, and retrieve properties and their values. For simplicity, JS API should work on the schema level. Schema class should be created:

class Schema { id; name; parentSchema; appliesTo }

```
grok.data.props.getSchemas(): Schema[]
grok.data.props.setValue(type: string, id: string, property: Property, value: dynamic)
grok.data.props.setAllValues(schema, keys: Column[], values: DataFrame)
grok.data.props.getAllValues(schema: Schema, keys: Column): DataFrame
grok.data.props.saveSchema(schema: Schema)
grok.data.props.deleteSchema(id: uid)
```



## UI
Self-service UI will be provided for creating properties/schemas, associating them with 

### Context panel
If a cell has custom properties, they are shown in the context panel. Values might be editable as well.

### Batch retrieval
If a column has associated schemas, a “Get properties” action is shown in the column context panel. If multiple schemas are associated, a dialog with the checkboxes shows up. This action adds a column for each property, and fills it with the retrieved values (see JS API: getAllValues). Depending on the privileges and settings, values could be edited right in the grid. 

### In-grid editing 
If a grid already has db property columns, in-grid editing might be available, subject to privileges and settings. Two modes of editing could be supported: automatic sync whenever you change a value, or the “SAVE” button for batch saving that would appear on the ribbon panel when you edit a db property.

### Tooltips and cell augmentation
Grid cells that have db properties will be rendered with a small triangle in the right top corner.
Db properties will be shown in the tooltip as well.

## Persistence
To avoid confusion, the values in the columns containing db properties should not be serialized as part of the project; instead, they should be re-queried each time a project is open.

# Open Questions & Future Roadmap

## Audit
If necessary, the history of modification will be provided using the built-in audit capability. This feature fits well with the proposed design and can be added after the MVP.

## Multiple Key Columns
Cell-based db properties are quite powerful, simple and intuitive, but sometimes entity key is contained in multiple columns (example: entity type is “plate well”, key columns: “plate barcode” and “well position”. In this case, the entity type notation would follow special syntax like “[semType:plate barcode, semType: well position]”. This complicates both the UI and entity resolution a bit, but still fits with the proposed design, so it can be added after the MVP.

## Entity Key Resolver
Sometimes, the natural key is not contained in the cell itself, but could be inferred from it (perhaps using other columns as well). An example is using canonical smiles as a key for molecules. To address this, we will use special “entity resolver” functions. This feature fits well with the proposed design and can be added after the MVP.

```
//input: list ids
//output: list keys
//meta.sourceSemType: BMol
//meta.targetEntityKey: BMol
keys = ids.map((id) => convert(id));
Special Property Types
```

Some properties can be quite universally useful, so we need to make them available in advance. In particular, File attachment, 5-star rating and a discussion. These will require a special UI:
* Attach a file to an entity, with d&d or upload dialogue. Can restrict file types for security. Can attach multiple files. Files with the same file name will be versioned. An attachment icon will be visible on the entity
* Ability to assign a star rating to an entity by clicking on a star. Show the average rating on the entity.
* Start a discussion about an entity. Everybody who participates in the discussion as well as the entity owner (if it exists) are notified about new comments.

issues.title: #2667: MSA: Use Mafft for nucleotide MSA
issues.body:
# Background

The JnJ team requested using [Mafft](https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/server/index.html) for DNA/RNA sequence alignment.
# Scope of work
* Implement running MSA via Mafft
* Add UI to choose alignment method (KAlign/Mafft) for macromolecules MSA.

# Details
## How to install Mafft
* Bioconda: conda install bioconda::mafft
* Binary deb package: wget https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/mafft_7.520-1_amd64.deb
* Source code: https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/installation_without_root.html
  
# Sample data
http://www.lbgi.fr/balibase/BalibaseDownload/BAliBASE_R10.tar.gz

Two sample files form this benchmark are attached to this ticket
# Running Mafft
**Fast run with default options**
```mafft BBA0001.tfa > BBA0001.mafft.fasta```

**Slower run with iterative refinement**
```mafft --genafpair --maxiterate 1000 BBA0001.tfa > BBA0001.mafft.E-INS-i.fasta```

issues.title: #2716: Having a Fixed10() math function in addition to Round10() would be useful
issues.body:
I wanted to build a `YYYY.MM` string out of a date. I thought of using this formula:
```
ToString(Year(${First Synthesis Date}) + 0.01 * Month(${First Synthesis Date}))
```
but of course it does not play well with October:
![image](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/assets/5244385/44da28a5-82da-4135-b89f-d8bd7f8a62f9)
`Round10` does not help, as it will truncate but not pad:
```
ToString(Year(${First Synthesis Date}) + 0.01 * Round10(Month(${First Synthesis Date}), 2))
```
So a `Fixed10()` math function would be useful (we discussed something similar for column formats, but I think also this use case deserves attention).

By the way, I also tried the following alternative approach, but `PadLeft` does not seem to work (see #2715):
```
ToString(Year(${First Synthesis Date})) + "." + PadLeft(ToString(Month(${First Synthesis Date})), 2, "0")
```

So I ended up with the rather cumbersome
```
ToString(Year(${First Synthesis Date})) + "." + If(Length(ToString(Month(${First Synthesis Date}))) == 1, Add("0", ToString(Month(${First Synthesis Date}))), ToString(Month(${First SynthesisDate})))
```
which works as expected:
![image](https://github.com/datagrok-ai/public/assets/5244385/1ecff960-370a-4369-9533-57c342df44bb)

#2872: RFC: Public API
issues.body:
The goal of the document is to provide context to public api initiative.

### Context and goals:

Datagrok currently has a server api and js api, which are not intended for external use. However, there are client needs for integration with datagrok. For example, ability to upload dataframes and set up dashboards programmatically.

We aim to create a public REST API and a wrapper in python so clients are able to include datagrok in their data pipelines.

#### Use case 1: pipeline-generated dashboards
Tim has a pandas dataframe that he wants to upload to Datagrok, apply some visualization, and share with other users as part of the data pipeline. With python wrapper he will be able to upload the dataframe to Datagrok with his favorite configuration previously exported in “.layout” format.

#### Use case 2: cross-language scripts
Steve has written a Datagrok R script, and shared it with the users so it can be interactively used via Datagrok. Now, he wants to be able to easily call that script from his Python code.
#### Use case 3: parameterized queries
Ed has created a connection to the database, and wrote a number of pretty complex parameterized queries. He wants to let data scientists make the same queries from Python. 
#### Use case 4: files
Ability to access and manipulate files in the file shares

### Authentication
Authentication will use API key taken from user summary (eg http://localhost:8889/u/admin/summary)
This key will be passed in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

### Routing
All public requests will be going through /public/v1/* endpoints so they can be easily distinguished and versioned.
##Work with files
Tables will use namespaced names for identification. Example can be “project.dashboard.table”
For files we should pass a connection identifier and path to a file. Example can be “System.DemoFiles/chem%2Fsmiles.csv”

In v1, we support single table download/upload, so it can be done with uploading a single csv/parquet file. In future we can extend this with downloading/uploading in zip 

When tables are uploaded, a dashboard can be created as a set of tables and a layout file.

## Functions
To enable invoking functions, the platform should be able to identify a function by its namespaced name. As for passing arguments, we plan to support primitive data types as well as columns/data frames through their identifiers, matching the upload/download identifiers

### OpenAPI
We will expose API with openAPI specification so it can be imported easily to clients projects with codegen.

## Planned API v1

```
HTTP GET /public/v1/tables/{name} - download table by namespaced `name`
HTTP GET /public/v1/tables/{connector}/{path} - download table from `connector` located in `path`
HTTP POST /public/v1/tables/{name} - upload table as csv/parquet body and save it to `name`, 
HTTP POST /public/v1/tables/{connector}/{path} - upload table as csv/parquet body and save it to `connector` under `path`, 
HTTP POST /public/v1/tables/share/{id}/{group}?mode="view/edit" - share table `id` with `group` and give permission to view/edit based on mode.

HTTP POST /public/v1/dashboards/{name}/{table_id1},{table_id2},{...} - create dashboard `name` that has tables `table_1`, `table_2`, .... Layout can be uploaded in body.

HTTP POST /public/v1/call/{name} - call function `name` with arguments passed in JSON key-value body.

HTTP GET /public/v1/files/{connector}/{path} - download file from `connector` located in `path`
HTTP POST /public/v1/files/{connector}/{path} - upload file to `connector` under  `path`
```

## Python wrapper example

```python
import datagrok as dg
from sklearn.datasets import load_titanic


dg.token = 'Bearer …'
dg.url = 'http://localhost:8082'


### === FILES ===


# identify everything with nqName
# if we do python wrapper, result probably should be pandas
df = dg.download_table('System:DemoFiles/chem/smiles.csv')
# # or
# df = dg.download_table('clinicalcase.clindemofiles2/tv')


# some processing
df[0, 'Severity'] = 'High'

# Upload tables to either personal or public namespace
# Can also be saved to connector
df_id = dg.upload_table(df, 'smiles-new')
titanic_id = dg.upload_table(load_titanic(), 'System:DemoFiles/titanic.csv')

# Create a dashboard from dataframes with a given layout
dashboard_id = dg.upload_dashboard([df_id, titanic_id], prefix_name='core:api_demo',
                        layout='pretty.layout')

# sharing with usergroup or users, specifying namespace if needed
dg.share(dashboard_id, 'Researchers', access='edit')
dg.share(dashboard_id, 'core:Kamelichev', access='view')


### === CALLS ===


# params are serialized as json
dg.call('UsageAnalysis:TestCount', {
 'date': '21-05-2024'
})


# Column, dataframe, column list can be passed as arguments
# We can return dataframes and columns from calls
extracted_df = dg.call('core:ExtractColumns', {
 'df': df_id,
 'columns': ['USUBJID', 'AGE']
})
calculated_column = dg.call('core:ExtractValue', {
 'df': titanic_id,
 'column': 'AGE',
 'function': 'core:Abs'
})

'''
# Some fancy wrappers could also be done
proj = dg.project([df], layout='layouts/pretty_one.layout')
proj.add(datasets.load_titanic())
proj.addViewer(DG.VIEWER.BAR_CHART, {
 "valueColumnName": "SUBJID",
 "valueAggrType": "count",
 "barSortType": "by value",
 "barSortOrder": "desc",
 "splitColumnName": "DTHFL"
})
'''



```

issues.title: #2910: Heatmap | Memory issue when heatmap contains molecule columns
issues.body:
v1.18, 1.19

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open a table with molecules, e.g. SPGI
2. Open filters (not sure if necessary, but it looks to worsen the issue)
3. Add a heatmap
4. Configure heatmap to contain Structure and R groups columns
5. Adjust vertical zoom slider on heatmap, move it up and down OR change heatmap viewer size so that it is re-rendered
6. Monitor memory used by the browser page

**Expected results:** heatmap is re-rendered without issues or warnings. There should be no memory leaks and out of memory crashes.
**Actual results:** Page freezes for a while and multiple warnings appear in the console:
`Molecule not rendered due to width or height less than 1`
Page starts to take more and more memory on re-rendering the heatmap (when vertical zoom is adjusted or viewer size is changed).
For some larger datasets page eventually crashes with 'out of memory' error.

issues.title: #3009: Calculated column hints break with round bracket + curly bracket
issues.body:
1. Load [qnum.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16759988/qnum.csv) into  native DG
2. Open browser dev console
3. From the menu, pick Edit->Add New Column
6. Call the column `test`
7. Start typing `if(${I`, then pick the `Id` hint: the dev console fills with errors:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c01a134-9ae3-4977-ae9b-0ee21c355a37)
8. Now type comma, and then space: when you hit space, the `${Id}` parameter disappears (see #2981)
9. From this point, it is impossible to type anything unless you reposition the cursor after each keystroke.

The only way to recover is to cancel the dialog and restart from scratch _without_ adding the curly bracket after the `$`.

Note that the trigger of the bug is the presence of an open round bracket _and_ an open curly bracket.
The open round bracket alone does not cause problems if `$` is not followed by open curly bracket.
Similarly, the open curly bracket after `$` does not cause problems unless it is preceded by an open round bracket.

It looks like the problem lies in the bookkeeping of brackets, as in #2981.

issues.title: #3010: Qnum does not seem to work in connection with if
issues.body:
I would like to enter a formula that conditionally computes a qualified pIC50, but it does not seem to work.

1. Load [qnum.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16760234/qnum.csv) into native DG
2. Open dev console and create a few calculated columns:
```
table = grok.shell.tableByName('qnum')
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('IsLesserThan', 'eq(Qualifier(${IC50 (uM)}), \'<\')', 'bool')
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('IsGreaterThan', 'eq(Qualifier(${IC50 (uM)}), \'>\')', 'bool')
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('IsExact', 'eq(Qualifier(${IC50 (uM)}), \'=\')', 'bool')
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('pIC50', 'if(${IsLesserThan}, Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'>\'), if(${IsGreaterThan}, Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'<\'), Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'=\')))', 'qnum')
```
I would have expected that the `pIC50` column showed a `qnum` with inverted qualifier compared to the `IC50 (uM)` column, but that does not seem to work.
Outside the `if` things work as expected:
```
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('QualifierWithoutIf', 'Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'<\')', 'qnum')
```
The `QualifierWithoutIf` column shows all numbers with`<`, as expected.
If I try to put the above into an `if`, it fails:
```
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('QualifierWithIf', 'if(true, Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'<\'), Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'>\'))', 'qnum')
```
Obviously in principle the intermediate columns are unnecessary, I just wanted to try to break down the issue a bit; the formula below should work in isolation, but it does not:
```
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('pIC50', 'if(eq(Qualifier(${IC50 (uM)}), \'<\'), Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'>\'), if(eq(Qualifier(${IC50 (uM)}), \'>\'), Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'<\'), Qnum(-Log10(${IC50 (uM)}*1.0e-6), \'=\')))', 'qnum')
```

For an even simpler test:
```
await table.columns.addNewCalculated('test', 'if(true, Qnum(1, \'>\'), Qnum(1, \'<\'))', 'qnum')
```

issues.title: #3142: Viewers: Scatter plot: add ability to define columns for scatter plot whiskers
issues.body:
Add ability to define columns for scatter plot whiskers, e.g. to show StdDev.



Auto detection is applied only if dataset contains at least one min/max.range numerical column in addition to main axis (x or y) numerical column. Opening scatter plot the detection firstly searches only min-max column group, and if only one or non of two are present, looks for range column then.  Otherwise (in no columns by name is found) search by tag is preformed. When view is opened, along with selecting main axis columns (x or y axis column), its min/max/range columns are searched automatically (same way when the view is opened); works only if auto detection is applied before.



To be detected, whisker columns must start with main axis column name, then optionally goes “whisker“ or “error“ suffix and then a type: min/max/range. For example, if axis column “col1“ in a dataframe has some whisker columns to match like “col1 min“, “col1 whisker max“, “col1 error range“, then min/max pair will be found for the axis column and “col1 min“, “col1 whisker max“ will be applied as whisker min & max columns. If only “col1 whisker max“ (or “col1 min“) , “col1 error range“ are present, then range column will be detected. if only one of min-max pair is present or none of columns, then nothing is detected.



Detection tags can be added to an axis column and contain a key with optional suffix (“whisker“) and type like min/max/range and exact whisker column name as a value.



Min or/and max columns have higher priority to be displayed (if any/two of then is/are selected) than range column.

issues.title: #3232: Integrate Boltz-1
issues.body:
Integrate the **Boltz-1** open-source model to enable state-of-the-art biomolecular structure prediction. This integration will facilitate seamless inference by allowing users to select YAML schemas and retrieve predicted structures.  

For more details, refer to the Boltz-1 GitHub [page](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz)

**Integration Scope:**  

1. **Server-side implementation:**  
   -Accept YAML schema input.  
   - Run inference using the command:  
     ```bash
     boltz predict input_path --use_msa_server
     ```
   - Process and return the predicted biomolecular structure.  
 

2. **Client-side implementation:**  

   - Maintain a folder containing predefined YAML schemas.  
   - Provide a dialog interface for users to select a schema.  
   - Send the selected schema to the server and retrieve the predicted structure.

issues.title: Grid: Selection and deselection improvements
issues.body:
**User request:**
Be able to select disconnected row and column ranges, as one would do in Excel or Spotfire. It should be easier to compose disconnected selections as this is something users need on a daily basis.

**Details:**

_**Case 1:**_

1. In Excel, the user can CTRL+click on row 2, SHIFT-click on row 4, then CTRL+click on row 8, shift click on row 10 and I will get the disconnected range 2-4,8-10 selected
2. In Spotfire, the user can do the same by pressing CTRL+SHIFT rather than just SHIFT
3. In Datagrok, the user cannot seem to be able to do this, neither for rows nor for columns.
- For rows, one can select 2-4, then select 8, when the user tries to select 8-10 it will always select the whole 2-10 range, which is not what they want.
- For columns, range selection does not work at all: If the user presses SHIFT, it will add only the column they click on to the range selection (as if they had pressed CTRL), which is unexpected.
- Interestingly, CTRL and SHIFT still behave differently on column selection, as with SHIFT one can add individual columns to the selection, but the user cannot remove from selection: only CTRL works for deselecting.

_**Case 2:**_
Also, it should be possible to click on the topmost cell (as in Excel) to clear the selection, while clearing a selection is quite cumbersome at the moment.

issues.body: User-Friendly Filtering and Pivoting: Toxicologists often want to slice data by subgroups – e.g., view only males, or only the high-dose group, or exclude an animal that was deemed an outlier (sometimes one animal might be sick due to non-drug reasons). Datagrok’s interactive filters and linking would be a killer feature here. Unlike static tools, the user can dynamically include/exclude animals or time points and see the results update across all views. This exploratory freedom is something traditional tools (Excel or static SAS plots) cannot offer easily.

issues.title: Clinical/Preclinical Case: Free scripting capability
issues.body: Automation and Scripting: Advanced users might want to do custom analyses (e.g., apply a specific statistical test or generate a custom plot). Because Datagrok allows integration of R/Python scripts in the workflow, a killer feature could be letting users run custom computations on the SEND data within the app. For example, a user could run an R script to perform a Dunnett’s test for each lab parameter comparing doses to control, and then show the p-values in the UI. While not out-of-the-box for all users, the ability to extend the analysis (for those with coding skills) means the tool can be adapted to specific company needs – a big plus for differentiating the platform.

issues.title: Clinical/Preclinical Case: Fast search across different studies
issues.body: Scalability and Data Integration: Pharma companies might have hundreds of studies stored. A Datagrok-based solution could connect to a data warehouse or repository of SEND datasets (instead of handling one study at a time). If Datagrok indexes the data, it could enable fast search (e.g., find all occurrences of a particular histopathology term across studies). This enterprise integration – being able to ingest data from file shares or databases automatically – leverages Datagrok’s strengths and would save users time in aggregating data.

issues.title: Clinical/Preclinical Case: Insights/recommendations
issues.body:
In general, preclinical toxicology analysis benefits from any feature that makes the review faster and findings clearer. Toxicologists often ask: "What happened and at what dose?" A well-designed SEND analysis plugin should quickly answer: Which organs were affected? How did clinical pathology values change? Was it dose-dependent? Did it onset early or only after chronic dosing? 
Several implementation options: (1) Insights tab with viewers with relevant presets based on [hidden] calculated columns; (2) Insights info pane with tabs (same approach), (3) KPI widgets.

issues.title: Add showSelectedRows property to Scatterplot viewer
issues.body:
## Summary
Added a `showSelectedRows` boolean property (default `true`) to the Scatterplot viewer that controls whether selected markers are visually highlighted using `selectedRowsColor`.

## Motivation
Users need the ability to disable selection highlighting in scatterplots while maintaining selection state for filtering and other operations. This is particularly useful when:
- Using color coding by a column and wanting to see those colors even for selected rows
- Creating visualizations where selection state should not affect the visual appearance
- Maintaining consistency with other viewers that offer similar control

## Implementation
The property follows the established pattern used in Bar Chart and Pie Chart viewers (both have `showSelectedRows` property).

### Changes Made

**1. scatterplot_look.dart**
- Added `@Prop(category: 'Selection')` annotated `showSelectedRows` property (default `true`)
- Placed in Selection category alongside related properties

**2. scatterplot_core.dart**
- Modified `getColor()` method (2 locations) to check `look.showSelectedRows` before returning `selectedRowsColor`
- When disabled, falls through to normal color coding logic

**3. scatterplot_renderer.dart**
- Modified `_renderMarkers()` method to check property before redrawing selected markers on top
- When disabled, selected markers drawn in normal z-order

**4. Code generation**
- Ran `dart build.dart` to generate property descriptors
- Property now accessible via `scatterPlot.props.showSelectedRows`

## Behavior

### When showSelectedRows = true (default)
- Current behavior maintained - selected markers use `selectedRowsColor` (orange)
- Selected markers drawn on top for visibility
- Backward compatible with existing layouts

### When showSelectedRows = false
- **No color column:** Selected markers use `filteredRowsColor` (blue)
- **Categorical column:** Selected markers show their category color
- **Numerical column:** Selected markers show their gradient color
- Selected markers drawn in normal z-order (not on top)
- Selection state still affects other app features (filters, statistics, etc.)

## Files Modified
- `lib/src/scatterplot/scatterplot_look.dart` (1 property added)
- `lib/src/scatterplot/scatterplot_core.dart` (2 lines modified)
- `lib/src/scatterplot/scatterplot_renderer.dart` (1 line modified)
- `lib/src/scatterplot/scatterplot.g.dart` (auto-generated)

## Testing
Property appears in Settings panel under Selection category and correctly controls selection visualization behavior.

issues.title: Grid: Support aggregation and visualization of vector values stored in cells
issues.body:
Datagrok's data engine already supports storing dataframes inside dataframe cells, which makes it efficient to represent multiple values per cell (e.g., three IC50 measurements: 12, 15, 18 nM for a single compound). However, there is currently no UI for visualizing such vectors or for applying column-level aggregations over them.

**Scope**
Implement UI support for dataframe-in-cell values, including:

- Cell rendering — display all raw values within a single cell (not just a summary).
- Column-level aggregation — configurable aggregation function per column (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, median, min, max, count, stdev, etc.), switchable on the fly.
- Aggregate-driven operations — the selected aggregation should drive:

  - sorting
  - filtering
  - plotting (viewers consume the aggregated value)
  - MPO (Multi-Parameter Optimization) scoring


- Persistence — aggregation choice should be saved with the layout/project.

issues.title: DateDiff and UnixTimestamp return incorrect/inconsistent values in calculated columns
issues.body:
The DateDiff function in Datagrok calculated columns returns incorrect, inconsistent, and sign-wrong results when computing the difference between a date column and a fixed reference date. UnixTimestamp exhibits the same problem.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open an analysis
2. Create a calculated column using:

DateDiff(${<SomeDateColumn>}, Date(2026,5,19))


3. Observe values for different dates in the column:

5/1/2026 20:20:56 → -1481943994: negative, plausibly sign-correct (May 1 is earlier than May 19), but magnitude seems wrong
4/8/2026 19:32:27 → 822914973: positive, should be negative (April 8 is even earlier than May 1)
3/25/2026 13:43:21 → -407631104: negative but smaller absolute value than the May 1 result, though March 25 is further from the reference date

Results are non-monotonic and sign-inconsistent across dates. Using UnixTimestamp as a workaround yields equally bogus results.

Expected behavior:
DateDiff(d1, d2) returns a consistent, monotonic, sign-correct time span (positive if d1 > d2, negative if d1 < d2), in a documented unit.

Actual behavior:
Values are inconsistent in sign and magnitude. Dates that are further in the past from the reference date do not produce larger negative differences.

Workaround (confirmed by reporter):
Use Year and DayOfYear to manually compute the elapsed time. This confirms the date values themselves are parsed correctly — the bug is in DateDiff / UnixTimestamp arithmetic.

issues.title: Proteomics: reconsider the default DE-path missing-value imputer (MinProb → KNN)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Proteomics differential-expression (DE) pipeline defaults its missing-value imputer to
**MinProb** (`packages/Proteomics/src/analysis/imputation.ts` — `showImputationDialog`,
`value: 'MinProb'`). MinProb fills missing values with a strongly down-shifted normal draw
(Perseus default: mean − 1.8·SD). That is the right model when a value is missing because the
protein is genuinely **absent** in a condition (left-censored MNAR, on/off). It is the **wrong**
model for the common case — partially-missing proteins that are present in both groups with some
random dropout — where imputing a low value corrupts the group mean/variance and destroys DE
power. On an n=4-per-group design a single down-shifted fill can sink a protein.

Proposing we reconsider the default for the DE path.

## Evidence (HYE spike-in, organism = ground truth)

Benchmark on the shipped `files/demo/spectronaut-hye-mix.tsv` (HYE two-proteome standard, 4 vs 4;
human = null, yeast 2:1 and E. coli 3:1 = true positives). Faithful to the real dialog: inject
missingness → apply the "min valid values per group" pre-filter (threshold 2) → impute → client
DE (Welch + BH) at |log2FC| ≥ 0.58, p ≤ 0.05. Recall is scored against the **original** 60 true
proteins (removed proteins count as not-recovered). 5-seed mean.

Baseline (complete data): recall 0.90, human FPR 0.03, null median log2FC 0.02.

| Missingness | Rate | **MinProb** recall | KNN recall | Mixed recall | MinProb null medFC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MCAR | 20% | **0.12** | 0.83 | 0.81 | 0.14 |
| MCAR | 35% | **0.03** | 0.64 | 0.65 | 0.13 |
| MNAR | 20% | **0.16** | 0.82 | 0.81 | 0.13 |
| MNAR | 35% | **0.04** | 0.62 | 0.66 | 0.26 |

- The min-valid pre-filter removes ≤ ~3 proteins here, so MinProb's collapse is **mis-imputation of
  partial holes**, not filtering.
- MinProb keeps FPR ≈ 0 — it isn't producing false positives, it's **silently losing almost all
  power** and skewing the null. A user sees "no errors" and doesn't realize ~90% of real hits are
  gone.
- **KNN** degrades gracefully and keeps the null unbiased (medFC ≤ 0.07); **Mixed** (MNAR fill for
  group-wise-absent cells, KNN for the rest) ≈ KNN. Mixed's theoretical edge barely shows because
  HYE's true positives are graded (2:1 / 3:1), not on/off, so there is little genuine group-wise
  absence to exploit.

## Recommendation

1. **Change the DE-path default imputer from MinProb to KNN.** Robust to partial missingness (the
   common case), unbiased null, gracefully degrading recall.
2. **Keep MinProb available** — it remains correct for genuine on/off absence (protein missing in an
   entire condition). Consider adding a short tooltip/README note on when each applies.
3. **Keep the "min valid values per group" pre-filter** — it does useful work (drops untestable
   proteins) and is orthogonal to the imputer choice.
4. **Later (not now):** a mechanism-aware **mixed** default (MNAR for group-wise-absent cells, KNN
   for partial) is the textbook ideal, but showed no measurable gain over plain KNN on this data.
   Worth revisiting on a peptide-poorer / on-off-heavy dataset that actually stresses the MNAR case.

## Open questions

- Does this hold on real client datasets with more genuine on/off absence (where MinProb is
  appropriate)? HYE understresses that regime.
- Should the default adapt to the detected missingness pattern (per-protein group-wise absence →
  MNAR fill; else KNN) rather than a single global method?

## Context

Surfaced while validating the report path against HYE ground truth. A regression test now guards the
clean-data operating point (`packages/Proteomics/src/tests/hye-ground-truth.ts`), and a related
`detectLog2Status` log2-skip bug on low-dynamic-range reports was fixed in the same effort
(commit 4693b12b30). Full analysis and the reproducible benchmark are in the report-path validation
deliverables.

issues.title: Proteomics: add preranked GSEA as a threshold-free complement to ORA enrichment
issues.body:
## Summary

Proteomics term enrichment is **ORA-only** today — `enrichmentAnalysis` calls g:Profiler's
g:GOSt (`src/analysis/enrichment.ts`) on the thresholded significant-gene hit list, split by
direction. ORA is set-based and threshold-sensitive: a protein counts fully in or fully out once
it crosses the significance cut, so a handful of borderline proteins can move a whole term. Propose
adding **preranked GSEA** as a complementary, threshold-free enrichment method.

## Why (evidence from a real client analysis)

On the Cytokinetics DMD/WT data we compared enrichment built from two DE paths (Spectronaut
"candidates" vs our recomputed "report" path). The two hit lists agree ~90% (κ=0.90), and pathway
conclusions agree — **except** for four DMD-relevant terms (interstitial matrix, elastic fibres,
growth factor activity; regulation of calcium ion transport) that were significant in one path and
not the other. The flip was driven entirely by ~a handful of boundary proteins crossing the DE cut,
amplified by ORA's all-or-nothing counting.

A one-off preranked GSEA (gseapy, ranking = log2FC) on the same data, run on **both** paths:

- **NES concordance between the two paths: Spearman 0.965** across 4,131 gene sets (vs ORA, where
  the four terms flipped). The path-dependence essentially disappears.
- The four flip terms become **path-robust**: e.g. elastic fibres NES −1.44 vs −1.45, growth factor
  activity −1.52 vs −1.53, calcium transport +1.49 vs +1.59 — near-identical either way, directions
  consistent with ORA.
- Bonus finding: under GSEA those terms are **sub-significant** (FDR 0.14–0.42), i.e. ORA's
  significance for them in the report path was partly a threshold artifact. GSEA is both
  path-robust *and* less prone to overstating marginal terms.

Repro: `~/Downloads/ck/analysis_scripts/gsea_concordance.py` (analysis deliverables, not in-repo).

## Proposal

Add preranked GSEA alongside ORA (complement, not replace):

- **Engine:** server-side script — `fgsea` (R, matches the existing limma/DEqMS/VSN R-script +
  client-fallback pattern) or `gseapy`/`blitzgsea` (Python). g:Profiler's API can't do preranked GSEA.
- **Input:** the full ranked DE result (all proteins, signed metric — log2FC or sign·−log10p), not a
  hit list. Needs tie/missing handling and a gene-set DB (MSigDB / GO / KEGG / Reactome).
- **Output schema:** Term, ES, NES, NOM p, FDR, leading-edge genes, Direction (sign of NES).
- **Viewers — largely already built.** The Phase 19 enrichment aids map almost 1:1 onto GSEA output:
  signed NES ↔ the directionality bar, and leading-edge is native to GSEA (the current leading-edge
  drill-down is an ORA-intersection approximation of exactly this). Much of the UI investment is reusable.

## Implications / effort

- Heavier compute than ORA's instant hypergeometric (permutation-based) → server call, not client.
- New dependency (fgsea or gseapy) + gene-set DB handling + result schema + viewer wiring + tests.
- De-risked by the existing R-script infrastructure and the Phase 19 viewers.
- Positioning: keep ORA for fast, interactive "what's in my hit list"; GSEA for robust, threshold-free
  conclusions. Offer both; flag when they disagree.

## Open questions

- fgsea (R) vs gseapy/blitzgsea (Python) — which fits the deploy story best?
- Ranking metric default (log2FC vs signed −log10p vs moderated-t) and how to expose it.
- Gene-set source/versioning and organism handling (reuse the enrichment organism setting).

Sibling to #3930 (imputer-default rethink) — both are method-quality improvements surfaced by the
Cytokinetics report-path validation.

issues.title: Chem: Substructure Search: Add an option to delay the filtering until sketcher confirmation
issues.body:
Currently, substructure search results are updated dynamically while the structure is being edited in the sketcher. This can cause the reference compound list to change before the final query structure is completed, making it difficult to build a query based on existing compounds in the table.

Add a checkbox option in the sketcher dialog to control filtering behavior:

- When enabled, keep the current behavior with live filtering during structure editing.
- When disabled, apply the substructure search only after clicking OK (or completing the sketcher action).

This allows users to construct complex queries step by step while keeping the original compound set available as a reference until the final structure is submitted.
